question: In organising the Rowlatt Satyagraha, Mahatma Gandhi was assisted by Abdul Bari of the Firangi Ulema group based in _________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Lucknow**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Mahatma Gandhi organized the Rowlatt Satyagraha in 1919 as a non-violent protest against the Rowlatt Act enacted by the British colonial government.
 
• The Rowlatt Act gave the British authorities sweeping powers to arrest and detain individuals without trial, which was widely criticized as repressive.
 
• Abdul Bari, a prominent figure from the Firangi Mahal Ulema group in Lucknow, played a significant role in assisting Gandhi in mobilizing support for the Satyagraha.
 
• The Firangi Mahal group, based in Lucknow, held substantial influence in the Muslim community and supported the idea of Hindu-Muslim unity against colonial oppression.
 
• The Rowlatt Satyagraha marked the beginning of Gandhi's larger campaign of nonviolent resistance against British rule in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rowlatt Act (1919):**

 
 
• Officially known as the Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act, it allowed detention without trial and curbed civil liberties.
 
• The act was opposed widely, leading to nationwide protests under Gandhi's leadership.
 
 
 
• **Jallianwala Bagh Massacre:**
 
 
• One of the most tragic events linked to the protests against the Rowlatt Act, where British troops opened fire on a peaceful gathering in Amritsar on April 13, 1919.
 
• This massacre became a turning point in India's struggle for independence, intensifying anti-British sentiments.
 
 
 
• **Non-Violent Civil Disobedience:**
 
 
• The Rowlatt Satyagraha was among the first large-scale demonstrations where Gandhi implemented his philosophy of Satyagraha (non-violent resistance).
 
• This approach later became the foundation of India's freedom struggle against British colonial rule.
 
 
 
• **Firangi Mahal:**
 
 
• A renowned Islamic seminary in Lucknow known for its contribution to Islamic education and jurisprudence.
 
• The Firangi Mahal Ulema group, including Abdul Bari, supported the Khilafat Movement and Gandhi's efforts to unite Hindus and Muslims against colonial rule.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Rowlatt Satyagraha:**
 
 
• Although the movement was withdrawn after incidents of violence, it marked the rise of Mahatma Gandhi as a mass leader in India's independence struggle.
 
• It also laid the groundwork for future movements like the Non-Cooperation Movement (1920-1922).
